claims.text: Combinatorial synthesis can be used to fabricate a library of HfNbTaTiZr alloys with systematically varied elemental percentages.
Changing the elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr will produce non-linear changes in mechanical properties.
Composition-induced changes in grain size contribute to changes in the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr.
Composition-induced changes in phase distribution contribute to changes in the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr.
The initial material is an as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy at a baseline composition.
Controlled processing and standardized heat treatments can minimize extraneous variability among the compositionally varied samples.
Small adjustments in HfNbTaTiZr elemental composition alter phase stability.
Small adjustments in HfNbTaTiZr elemental composition alter precipitate formation.
Changes in phase stability and precipitate formation modify the alloy's microstructural landscape.
The modified microstructure influences dislocation dynamics.
Changes in dislocation dynamics influence mechanical strength.
Slightly modified HfNbTaTiZr compositions will exhibit statistically significant differences in yield strength relative to the baseline.
Slightly modified HfNbTaTiZr compositions will exhibit statistically significant differences in ductility relative to the baseline.
The anticipated composition-property effects are expected to hold under similar processing conditions.
Extreme compositional or processing deviations may induce additional phases or effects beyond the anticipated trends.
